02 / The big idea

USEFUL THINGS.
MADE WITH CARE.

The pen that signs the paperwork. The knife carried every day. The razor before the shift. The ring that reminds you what you work for.

Not a random assortment of merchandise. One recognizable identity, expressed through practical objects, carefully selected materials, and work worth being proud of.

The reward for good work is more work.

04 / Where it started

THE FIRST PEN.
THE BIGGER IDEA.

This is a real pen made by Harry. The workmanship is already there: shaped material, a smooth finish, and carefully assembled hardware.

The idea isn't to replace what Harry does. It's to show how that same care could define an entire range of useful goods.

Real craftsmanship is the starting point.
The details / brand system

ONE MARK. EVERY OBJECT.

A restrained BCW mark can connect a pen clip, presentation box, shaving handle, ring case, and workwear patch. Each application needs a different manufacturing test.

01ENGRAVED HARDWARE

Test whether existing clips and metal components accept a clean, durable mark.

02WOOD & PACKAGING

Burn, laser, or stamp the mark where contrast and material performance permit.

03APPAREL & GOODS

Carry the same simplified mark into embroidery, woven patches, and printed drinkware.

05 / Materials and character

NO TWO PIECES ALIKE.

Explore the material families that could shape future products. Black Forest Wood Co. and other turning suppliers offer prepared blanks; individual material suitability depends on the project and kit.

Maple & figured burlUnique grain, distinctive finish
Resin hybridsBold colour, dramatic contrast
Stabilized woodSpecialty blanks for selected uses
Reclaimed lumberA second life for suitable shop offcuts
Gunmetal hardwareUnified details across collections

Matching gift setsShared materials across multiple objects

06 / From the worksite

WHAT'S LEFT
CAN MATTER.

Suitable clean lumber offcuts that would otherwise be discarded could become distinctive handmade pens and keepsakes.

This is a prototype concept. Wood selection, drying, turning performance, finishing and permission to recover materials all need to be confirmed before a reclaimed collection can be sold.

The work remains. So does the material.
07 / A thought for Harry

IMAGINE WHAT'S NEXT.

You've already made the pen. The next step is imagining what the same skills, materials and pride in workmanship could become.

Pens are where the story starts. They don't have to be where it ends.
